docs.text:
A Stencil theme built on Cornerstone by PapaThemes.

Start the install guide Browse every setting

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text:
This guide is written for store owners, not developers. Follow it from top to bottom and you will have a storefront configured the way you want it, without touching any code.

Ember Theme uses no external services and asks for no API keys — everything it renders comes from your own catalog and settings.

You will learn how to:

  1. Install and activate the theme.
  2. Pick the variation — Home, Fashion or Food — that matches the look you want.
  3. Work through the Theme Editor section by section.
  4. Set up the two features that need more than a checkbox: the Lookbook and the Page Builder hero.
  5. Use the four custom page templates: About, FAQ, Track Order and Lookbook.

docs.title: The three variations
docs.text:
Same features in all three. Each variation has its own layout preset as well as its own colour and type, and each is named for the kind of store it was designed for: Home & Garden, Fashion & Jewelry, or Food & Beverage.

Variation Layout preset What it looks like Demo Home Classic Logo left, split hero beside its copy, framed product cards four across, orange accent. The theme's own defaults. ember-home-demo Fashion Editorial Centred logo over the menu, full-bleed hero, three-across grid, display serif, brass accent, opens in dark mode. ember-fashion-demo Food Market Wide search on the top row with the aisles below, framed hero with the copy on the photo, round category tags, five-across home grids, herb green. ember-food-demo

Pick the variation first

Switching resets any setting the target variation defines. Choose the variation before you spend time on colours, or you will do that work twice.

docs.text: New settings were added and none removed or renamed, so installing over 1.1.27 keeps your configuration. Out of the box the home page hero shows the same three pills as before; nothing changes until you choose your own text.

docs.title: Home page
docs.text: • Hero pills: your own text, or none. In Theme Editor > Ember Theme > Homepage, Hero pills controls the three short notes under the hero buttons ("Free shipping", "30-day returns", "Secure checkout"). Choose Your text below to reword them in Pill 1 to Pill 3 (leave a pill empty to hide it), or Hidden to remove them. If your store charges shipping on some or all orders, change or hide the "Free shipping" pill. The same choice applies when the hero is built from your Control Panel carousel slides. See Hero pills.

docs.title: Blog
docs.text: • Blog cards line up. On the blog page and in the home page blog section, a post's tag now sits on the top-left corner of its photo instead of above the title, so every card's title starts at the same height. The author and date row and "Read more" sit at the bottom of each card, so a short excerpt no longer leaves them floating. A post without a thumbnail shows a soft placeholder in your accent colour, in the same frame as a photo, instead of an empty box; the featured post at the top of the blog page does the same.

docs.title: Cart and shipping
docs.text: • Free-shipping messages can be turned off everywhere. In Theme Editor > Ember Theme > Cart, Free Shipping Messages (formerly Shipping Bar) now controls every place the free-shipping amount appears: the top bar's default first message, the cart sheet, the product page, the cart page (shipping card and the "Free ship" badge) and the "On orders over" note in the home promo banner. Turn it off if your store ships free on every order, or has no free-shipping offer. Your own first top-bar message is always shown; when it is empty and the messages are off, the top bar starts with its second message. An amount of 0 is treated the same way. See Cart.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: • About page: your own hero sentence and closing banner. In Theme Editor > Ember Theme > About page, set Hero sentence and closing banner to Your text below to replace the sentence under the page heading and the closing "Ready to Shop?" banner with your own title, text and button. Button link takes a page of your store, such as /shop-all/; a link to another website opens your category list instead. Leave a field empty to hide that piece. The sample sentence promises shipping "everywhere", so change it if you ship to a few countries only. See About.

Without one, the photo now matches your style: a living room for Home, a clothes rail for Fashion and pantry jars for Food. See About.

docs.title: Cart
docs.text:
• Gift Certificate row: on stores that allow several promo codes per order (BigCommerce's newer cart summary), the cart summary has its own Gift Certificate row, next to the promo code row. Shoppers select Add to open a code field and Apply to redeem it, the same way the promo code works. The row is hidden when the shopper is browsing in a currency where gift certificates can't be used. Stores on the classic cart summary keep the gift certificate field as it was.
  • Promo code field: the field is now labelled "Promo code". It still accepts a gift certificate code.
  • Currency after switching: after a shopper switches currency, the cart now uses the currency they picked instead of the one they were in before.
  • Quantity buttons: tapping the − and + buttons on the product page, quick view, cart and cart drawer no longer flashes the browser's blue highlight; the button shows a pressed state in your theme's accent colour. Keyboard users still see the focus outline.

docs.title: Header
docs.text: • Search bar corners: the header search bar follows your theme's corner radius instead of always being fully rounded; the Fashion style keeps square corners. The search box on phones follows the same setting.

docs.text: • Category header banner: when a category has an image, the photo now sits behind the breadcrumb and title as a banner, with a shade that keeps the title easy to read. Choose the look in Theme Editor → Global → Products → Category header with an image: Banner (photo behind the title, the default) or Split (title beside the whole photo, as before). The Fashion style uses Split. See Category pages.

docs.title: Gift certificates

docs.text: • One scrollbar on category, brand and search pages: the filter sidebar now scrolls with the page instead of inside its own box, so a long filter list no longer shows a second scrollbar. It still stays in view while you scroll when it is short enough to fit under the header.

docs.title: Product page
docs.text:
• Quantity stepper: the quantity is now a box with − and + buttons, and shoppers can also type a quantity. There is no longer a limit of 20; the product's own minimum and maximum purchase quantities still apply. Quick view uses the same stepper.
  • Buttons fill on hover: the wishlist, compare and Buy Now buttons and the quantity − and + buttons fill with colour when you point at them, and Add to Cart turns a shade darker.
  • Tabs no longer jump: switching between Description, Specifications and Reviews keeps the tabs where they are instead of jumping the page.
  • Payment, trust and share block: the payment icons, trust badges and share buttons line up on one left edge with even spacing, and the Print share button has a border like the others.
  • Specifications: each value now sits right beside its label instead of at the far edge of the column.

docs.title: Cart
docs.text:

A store that already uses Food keeps the colours it has saved; it gets the new palette only when the Food variation is applied again with its original (default) settings, or when you set the colours yourself in Theme Styles.

docs.title: Food style: olive and cream
docs.text: • New default palette: the Food variation now uses deep olive (#4F5B2A) for buttons, links and the navigation band, on a fresh cream page (#FBF8F1), with tomato red (#C2401C) for sale badges and the flash-sale countdown. In dark mode the accent is a sage green. Before, Food was terracotta on beige and looked close to the Fashion style. Three new Food colour defaults are set for sale and warning colours; nothing else needs configuring.

docs.title: Category pages
docs.text: • Compact category header with the whole photo: the category title and description sit on the left and the category image on the right, at a fixed height (240px on desktop, 200px on tablets) and at its own shape, so nothing is cut off. On phones the image sits under the title. A category without an image or description shows only what it has, without an empty panel. The title size now matches the brand pages.

docs.title: Faster images
docs.text:
• Sized images instead of full-size originals: blog cards on the home page, the blog page and the blog post header, compare-table thumbnails and pattern swatch previews now load an image sized for where it is shown, instead of the full original upload.
  • Responsive theme images: the theme's own promo banners, Lookbook scenes and Lookbook room tiles load a size that fits the screen (400, 800 or 1200px wide, WebP where the browser supports it). Images you upload yourself are unchanged.

docs.title: Home page hero (Fashion and Food styles)
docs.text:
• More of the hero photo on wide screens: on screens wider than about 1320px, the home page hero in the Fashion and Food styles grows taller with the width, up to the height of the window below the header, instead of staying 620px tall and cutting off the top and bottom of the photo. In the Fashion style, when the window is too short to show the whole photo, more is cut from the bottom than the top, so heads and bag handles stay in view. Phones, tablets and narrower desktops look as before.
  • Your own carousel images: when the hero shows your Control Panel carousel, the shape of the first slide's image sets how tall the hero grows; a very wide banner image keeps the 620px height.
  • Fashion: copy centred: from 801px wide, the hero headline and buttons in the Fashion style sit in the middle of the photo's height instead of near the top.
  • With a banner above: when a marketing banner or a widget sits above the hero, the hero keeps its 620px height.

The Home style's hero is unchanged.

The image is drawn close to its own size, so it stays sharp; it is still cropped to fill its box, so a landscape image (around 3:2) with the subject in the middle works best. Phones keep the photo behind the text.
  • Same category tiles everywhere: the category tiles on the All Categories page now look the same as the home page tiles in each style. In the Fashion and Food styles that is the dark band with the white name on every photo; before, light photos on All Categories switched to a pale band with dark text.
  • Readable tile arrow: the arrow on category tiles keeps the name's colour on hover, so it stays easy to see in the Home and Fashion styles (the Food style has no arrow).
  • Filters: the Clear button in the filter sidebar appears only once a filter is set. On stores without product filtering, the price-only sidebar is more compact, and its Min field lines up with the Update button.

docs.text: Maintenance release. No setting or storefront text was added, removed or renamed, so installing over 1.1.0 keeps your configuration; there is nothing to configure.

docs.title: Readability
docs.text: • 12px minimum text size: every text in the theme is now at least 12px at every screen width, including the "Required" note on account forms, small labels, badges, the header cart and wish list counts, and printed invoices. The cart's trust tiles keep "Secure checkout" on one line.

docs.title: Phones and tablets
docs.text: • Larger tap areas: on touch screens up to 1024px wide, these controls now have 44px tap areas while looking the same: the wish list remove button and wish list actions, product colour swatches (including "None"), Lookbook markers, blog tags and categories, address Edit and Delete links, account menu and order filters, search result and FAQ tabs, the header logo on tablets and the Food hero arrows. Layouts with a mouse are unchanged.

docs.title: Footer
docs.text: • X icon for a social link named "X": a social media link named "x" now shows the X mark in the footer, as one named "twitter" already did, instead of a generic globe.

docs.title: 1.1.0 — 17 October 2026
docs.text:
Feature release. Installing over 1.0.7 keeps your configuration: no setting was removed or renamed. Three settings are new, under Theme Styles > Products > Featured promotions, and start with the values below. Two new storefront texts ship translated in every language file.

New setting Default Show featured promotions (show_featured_promotions) On Promotion background (yen-offer-bg-color) Home #FFF7ED, Fashion #F7F3EC, Food #FBEFE6 Promotion text (yen-offer-text-color) Home #B84600, Fashion #7A5D33, Food #8C3B26

docs.title: Featured Promotions
docs.text:
• Promotion callouts on products: when you feature an automatic promotion and give it a callout, the callout shows under the price on product cards (category, brand, search, home sections, related products, quick search), on the product page and in quick view. Cards show the top promotion and "+N more offers"; the product page and quick view list every one. Turn it off, or change its colours, in Theme Styles > Products > Featured promotions. Dark mode builds the callout colours from your Dark Mode Colors.
  • BigCommerce rollout: BigCommerce is enabling featured promotion data store by store. Until it is on for your store, no callouts appear, and nothing else changes.

docs.title: Backorders
docs.text:
• Backorders on the product page and in quick view: a product that can be backordered keeps Add to Cart when nothing is on hand (it is no longer labelled Sold Out), shows the availability prompt, how many units will be backordered and the product's backorder message (or your store's default message), and, for pick-list options, each option's own lines. A quantity above what can be sold disables Add to Cart with "The maximum purchasable quantity is N", also per pick-list option. The "Get it by" delivery estimate is withdrawn while any unit is backordered.
  • Backorders in the cart and orders: cart lines, in the cart page and the cart panel, show how many units are ready to ship, how many will be backordered and the backorder message, with a group per pick-list option, and the cart summary adds your shipping expectation when the cart holds a backordered item. Order details in My Account show the same lines under each product and the shipping expectation under the shipping address. What shows follows your Settings > Inventory choices. Backorder quantities appear only when Settings > Inventory > Stock level display is not "Don't show": BigCommerce sends no backorder figures while stock levels are hidden.

docs.title: Product page
docs.text: • Sold-out variant after an in-stock one: choosing a sold-out variant after an in-stock one now disables Add to Cart and shows Sold Out; the earlier variant's stock figure no longer carries over. A quick view opened over a product page reads its own product's stock, not the page product's.

docs.title: Shipping
docs.text: • No free-shipping promise next to a fixed shipping cost: a product with its own fixed shipping cost no longer shows the free-shipping bar on the product page; the line by Add to Cart states the cost instead. In the cart page and the cart panel, the free-shipping progress and "FREE" are left out when every product in the cart has a fixed shipping cost.

docs.title: Tablets
docs.text: • Larger tap areas on touch tablets: on tablets (768 to 1024px wide, touch screens), footer links, social icons, pagination, brand letters, grid/list toggles, the top-bar currency and light/dark buttons, product option chips and Lookbook markers have 44px tap areas. Layouts with a mouse are unchanged; the footer gets a little taller on tablets.

docs.title: Theme package
docs.text: • Image provenance: the theme package includes assets/PROVENANCE.md, which records how each bundled and demo image was made and its licence terms.

docs.title: 1.0.7 — 16 October 2026
docs.text: Maintenance release. No setting or storefront text was added, removed or renamed, so installing over 1.0.6 keeps your configuration; there is nothing to configure.

docs.title: Account
docs.text: • Wishlist Add to Cart readable in dark mode: on a wishlist page in dark mode, the Add to Cart button label was dark on the dark card and almost invisible, and in light mode its outline was very faint. The label, the outline and the hover fill now follow the colour mode. The Pre-order button and the stock note below it are easier to read too.

docs.title: 1.0.6 — 16 October 2026
docs.text: Maintenance release. No setting was added, removed or renamed, so installing over 1.0.5 keeps your configuration. Two new storefront texts, the promo code links in the cart panel below, ship translated in every language file; there is nothing to configure.

docs.title: Account
docs.text:
• Wishlist cards show the product again: on a wishlist page, the product photo no longer covers the card, so the name, the price and the Add to Cart button are visible and can be tapped.
  • Clearer "Required" labels: the "Required" note next to form fields is 12px at every screen width, the same as on phones.

docs.title: Currency
docs.text:
• Switching currency without a cart: choosing another currency before anything is in the cart now switches the store currency straight away, with no error in the browser console. With items in the cart, the cart changes to the new currency as before.
  • Fashion currency button: in the Fashion style, the currency button in the top bar is as large and easy to tap as in the Home style.

docs.title: Cart
docs.text:
• Promo codes in the cart panel: the cart panel now shows a link, "Have a promo code? Apply it in your cart" (or "promo code or gift card" when gift certificates are on), that opens the cart page, instead of a field that could not be typed in.
  • Easier quantity buttons: the - and + buttons in the cart panel have a larger tap area on phones and tablets, and with a mouse on small laptops; they look the same.
  • Remove confirmation in the theme style: removing an item from the cart panel asks for confirmation in the theme's own dialog, the same one the cart page uses, instead of the browser's plain pop-up. Pressing Escape closes the dialog and leaves the cart panel open.

docs.title: Food style
docs.text: • Readable reviews in dark mode: in the Food style in dark mode, the review date and the "Verified" badge on home page testimonials have stronger contrast.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
• Newsletter confirmation pages: the pages shown after subscribing, unsubscribing or creating an account no longer show a white band above the content panel.
  • Sale link: when no promo banner link is set, the home page promo button opens /sale/ directly, without a redirect.

docs.title: 1.0.5 — 15 October 2026
docs.text: Maintenance release. No setting was added, removed or renamed, so installing over 1.0.4 keeps your configuration. One new storefront text, the "Added to cart" heading below, ships translated in every language file; there is nothing to configure.

docs.title: Phones
docs.text:
• Newsletter sign-up in one row: in the footer and the home page newsletter band, the email field and its subscribe button now sit in a single row, with an arrow button inside the end of the field, instead of a field stacked over a full-width button. Tablets and desktops look as before.
  • Sign in first in the mobile menu: at the bottom of the menu drawer, Sign in is the filled main button and Register (Log out when signed in) the outlined one, and the drawer no longer ends in a band of empty space.
  • Closer hero slide dots: the slide dots on the home page hero are larger and closer together, each still easy to tap, and the pause button is easier to hit. Tablets and desktops look as before.
  • Calmer tap feedback: tapping a link or button no longer flashes a grey square over rounded chips and tiles. Category chips, category tiles and hero buttons show a brief colour change when pressed instead.

docs.title: Cart
docs.text: • "Added to cart" after adding: the cart panel that opens after Add to Cart is headed "Added to cart" with a check mark, so shoppers see at once that the item went in. Opened from the cart icon in the header it still reads "Your Cart".

docs.title: Product images
docs.text: • Image backgrounds blend in light mode: product photos on cards, in Quick View, on the product page and in the cart sit on a soft background matched to each style (Home, Fashion, Food), so photos shot on an off-white studio background no longer show as a separate pale box. Dark mode, banners, lookbook, category and brand images are unchanged.

docs.title: 1.0.4 — 15 October 2026
docs.text: Maintenance release. No setting was added, removed or renamed, so installing over 1.0.3 keeps your configuration.

docs.title: Header
docs.text: • The logo follows its size setting: a "Logo image size" other than the default 250x100 in the Theme Editor can now make the header logo larger, up to 80px tall on tablets and desktops, and the header row grows with it. Before, the logo was capped at 56px (44px in Fashion), so a larger size could only shrink it. The default size looks as before, and phones keep their 40px logo.

docs.title: Product cards
docs.text: • Keyboard users tab through a product card from top to bottom: the wish list, Quick View and compare buttons drawn on the product image come before the product name and the add to cart button. Nothing moves on screen.

docs.title: Category pages
docs.text: • A widget placed in the region below the product list (category_below_content) lines up with the products column beside the filter sidebar, spans the page where the filters are in the drawer, and no longer runs under the footer.

docs.title: Accessibility & touch
docs.text: • On touch screens, radio button labels in forms get a 44px tap row like the checkboxes, and the checkbox and radio boxes line up with the first line of their label.

docs.title: 1.0.3 — 15 October 2026
docs.text: Maintenance release. No setting was added, removed or renamed, so installing over 1.0.2 keeps your configuration.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• Two home page widget regions for Page Builder: home_above_products, directly above the first product feed (above the product tabs in Home and Fashion, above the New Arrivals shelf in Food), and home_above_footer, at the end of the page above the footer.
  • Quick View follows its setting: "Show quickview button on product cards" now removes the button everywhere when off. When on, the button also shows on touch tablets (768px and wider), including the narrow cards of the home tabs and Food shelves.
  • Share buttons follow the control panel: the product page shows the social sharing buttons you pick in the control panel, including Print and Facebook Like.

docs.title: Product page
docs.text:
• Adding to a wish list from the product page saves the item again; before, the request went out empty and nothing was added.
  • The wish list menu is no longer cut off on screens 860-1090px wide.
  • No "Get it by" delivery date on pre-order products.
  • A fixed shipping cost is shown in the shopper's currency.
  • Products with a price range show no strike-through price until a variant is chosen.
  • The free-shipping progress bar no longer counts the item just added twice.
  • A product with one image shows no thumbnail strip.
  • The review form fields line up, and the confirmation message scrolls into view after sending.

docs.title: Cart
docs.text:
• One "Promo code or gift card" box tries the code as a coupon, then as a gift certificate. In a currency other than your default it reads "Promo code", because BigCommerce only accepts gift certificates in the default currency. Applied gift certificates still list with Remove.
  • Order Summary: discounts on their own row, the shipping amount on one line, no "FREE" when every shipping option costs money, and a visible arrow in dark mode.
  • The cart lines up with the page title.
  • Escape closes the cart drawer and returns focus to the cart button.
  • Product Set widget dots on the cart page no longer show over the sticky header.
  • The free-shipping card matches the warm card colour in Food dark mode.
  • The gift certificate Remove link no longer touches its amount.

docs.title: Search & filters
docs.text:
• The filters sidebar is hidden on the News & Information search tab.
  • Brand pages: the price filter chip is formatted as currency, filtering down to no products shows the empty-results message, and stores without faceted search keep the Filters button and Shop by Brand drawer.
  • The /brands/ page uses the brand image size setting.

docs.title: Home & footer
docs.text:
• Hero slides: the old caption fades out before the new one appears.
  • Several marketing banners in one location no longer print a stray comma.
  • Promotion notices on the home page stay inside the page width.
  • The footer newsletter form shows on every page, uses your control panel newsletter summary when one is set, and tells shoppers who are already subscribed.
  • Home blog excerpts end on a whole word with an ellipsis.
  • Brand initial tiles are readable in dark mode.

docs.title: Account
docs.text:
• The Create Account tab is hidden when account creation is turned off.
  • Account pages: heading spacing on tablets and desktops, and the Email field styled like the other fields.

docs.title: Checkout and other pages
docs.text:
• Checkout, order confirmation, maintenance and hibernation pages keep the logo readable on dark headers: the dark-mode logo when set, otherwise a light plate behind the logo.
  • Web page content follows the body font size setting.
  • Products without an image show a sharp SVG placeholder.

docs.title: Accessibility & touch
docs.text:
• On touch screens, buttons and controls get a 44x44px tap area: main buttons, cart quantity, edit and remove, the sticky add to cart, home tabs, Lookbook card buttons, the filter drawer close button, card icons and share buttons. Mouse use on desktop is unchanged.
  • Better contrast for testimonial initials, Lookbook hotspot numbers and the gift certificate icon in dark mode.
  • The cart icon announces the item count with the right plural form in every language.
  • Compare page links and Product Set dots meet the minimum target size.
  • Cart item options are read as label and value pairs by screen readers.

docs.title: Mobile/tablet layout
docs.text:
• Lookbook "Choose options" buttons are no longer clipped at 761-820px in Fashion.
  • Long brand names on product cards wrap to two lines instead of being cut off; card rows stay aligned.
  • Compare page: a Sold Out label for sold-out products and star rows aligned across columns.
  • The product page share row wraps on small phones instead of being cut off.
  • Food shelves at 320px keep the stars and review count on one line.
  • The quick search panel on tablets lines up with the search field.
  • Currency menu title and Quick View brand text are slightly larger.

docs.title: Other
docs.text:
• The Outfit font is only loaded by the Home layout, so Fashion and Food pages load less.
  • New storefront texts are translated into all 20 languages; some are machine translations.
  • Marketplace descriptions corrected for the Home font and the Fashion header.

docs.title: 1.0.2 — 14 October 2026
docs.text: • Theme renamed from Yen to Ember. Settings, layouts and features are unchanged.

docs.title: 1.0.1 — 14 October 2026
docs.text: Maintenance release. No settings change; installing over 1.0.0 keeps your configuration.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Create account: every custom sign-up field you add in the control panel now shows. Fields whose name contained words such as "Birthday" or "Pay by PO" were hidden and lost their required flag.
  • Account menu: Messages and Recently Viewed are back in the account sidebar and on the dashboard.
  • Account dashboard: order, wish list and return counts are no longer capped at the number of items previewed; a long list shows "N+". The Addresses count, which BigCommerce does not provide on this page, was removed.
  • Account settings: Chrome no longer fills the saved password into New Password, which blocked saving a name or email change. The password fields sit in their own "Change password" group with a hint, and form fields carry the right autocomplete values.
  • Maintenance and hibernation pages: the browser tab shows the page heading instead of an empty title, and an empty favicon or logo is no longer printed.
  • Newsletter confirmation pages: buttons keep readable contrast on hover and focus in all three variations, light and dark; the breadcrumb names the current page. The default newsletter and home promo banner text no longer promises a fixed discount ("up to 30% off", "Up to 50% OFF") in any language.

docs.title: Other
docs.text: • Security patches to build tools. No storefront change.

docs.title: 1.0.0 — Initial release
docs.text: Yen Theme for BigCommerce, built on Cornerstone 6.19.0.

docs.title: Variations
docs.text:
Three, with the same features. Each has its own layout preset (Theme Editor → Yen Theme → Layout Preset) as well as its own colours and type.

  • Home — Classic layout, the theme's own defaults
  • Fashion — Editorial layout: centred logo, full-bleed hero, display serif, brass accent, opens in dark mode
  • Food — Market layout: search-first header, round category tags, five-across home grids, herb green, its own photographs and copy

docs.title: Shopping experience
docs.text:
• Home hero shows your Storefront → Carousel slides when you add them, in the theme's own hero design; without slides it shows the theme's three built-in slides
  • Dark/light mode toggle, with both modes designed rather than inverted
  • Mega navigation with featured images and multi-column layouts
  • Product cards with quick view, wishlist, compare and hover detail
  • Grid and list view on category, brand and search pages
  • Faceted search with a sidebar on desktop and a drawer on mobile
  • Cart page with a summary sidebar, shipping estimator and gift certificates

docs.title: The Lookbook
docs.text: Shoppable images: place hotspots on a photograph as percentage coordinates and map each one to a product ID. 41 settings, and a page template of its own.

docs.title: Custom page templates
docs.text: Four, each chosen from the template dropdown when creating a web page: Lookbook, About, FAQ and Track Order. All four render their own content — the page body you type is not what appears. See The other page templates for what that means in practice.

docs.title: Homepage
docs.text: Hero banner, trust badges, brand showcase, flash sale, reviews, press mentions and newsletter, each with its own on/off switch in the Theme Editor.

docs.title: Under the hood
docs.text:
• Full Page Builder and Theme Editor integration — 380 settings across 9 sections
  • Lazy loading with low-quality image placeholders, so images resolve in rather than jump
  • Responsive from phone to desktop, with the desktop layout starting at 1261px
  • Accessibility: ARIA attributes throughout, focus trapping in overlays, keyboard navigation, named landmarks, and a single main landmark per page
  • 20 storefront locales covering 13 distinct translations

docs.title: Phones and tablets
docs.text:
• Every page reworked for phones, tablets and phone landscape, in both colour modes, and readable at up to 200% text size
  • Add to Cart opens the cart as a sheet over the page instead of leaving the product
  • A per-slide Hero Focus (phones & tablets) setting keeps each hero photograph's subject in view when the picture is cropped — see Hero focus
  • One button system per layout preset, with the hover and pressed shades mixed from the Button colour

docs.title: Cart
docs.text:
• The cart page, the cart sheet and the product page say how much more qualifies for free shipping, in the shopper's currency
  • The cart page's cross-sell row leaves out products already in the cart
  • A promotion that splits a discounted unit onto its own line shows as one product, and minimum and maximum purchase quantities count across both lines

docs.title: Prices hidden from guests
docs.text: When the store hides prices from guests, no price reaches the page: not on product cards, bulk pricing tables, the product page's fixed shipping cost, the free-shipping bar, or the structured data search engines read. See Prices hidden from guests for what that means for Google rich results.

docs.title: Upgrading from a pre-release build
docs.text:
• Fonts: pick your body and heading fonts again so every weight loads — see Typography.
  • Primary button colour: #1B1D21, #333333 and #000000 in the Cornerstone primary button controls read as "not set" — see Primary button colour.

docs.title: What the theme does not do
docs.text:
• No external services and no API keys. Everything rendered comes from your own catalog and settings.
  • No order-lookup form on Track Order. BigCommerce provides no storefront endpoint a theme can query for a guest's order, so the page offers what does work: order history for signed-in shoppers, and the emailed tracking link for guests.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
A Lookbook product card is missing. The ID is wrong, or the product is not visible on the storefront. Check the ID in Products → View, and check the product is visible and in stock behaviour you expect.

A hotspot sits in the wrong place. Coordinates are percentages, not pixels, and they are measured against the image, not the screen. Re-check the pair order — dots map to product IDs by position.

Colours look wrong after switching variation. Switching applies that variation's settings over yours. Set the variation first, then customise.

Dark mode ignores a colour I changed. Dark mode has its own palette under Theme Editor → Ember Theme → Dark Mode Colors, and a colour changed under Colors does not carry over to it. Set both, and preview both modes before publishing.

The hero cuts off the person or product on a phone. The photograph is cropped to fit the narrow screen. Move the crop with Theme Editor → Ember Theme → Hero N Focus (phones & tablets) — see Hero focus.

I set a primary button colour and nothing changed. Each Cornerstone primary button control has one value the theme treats as "not set": #1B1D21 for the background, #333333 for hover, #000000 for pressed. Pick a colour one step away, such as #1B1D22, or set Ember Theme → Button instead — see Primary button colour.

Bold text looks smudged or too thin after an upgrade. The saved font setting loads a single weight. Pick the font again — see Typography.

Guests see no prices, and Google shows none either. The store is set to hide prices from guests, and the theme leaves prices out of the page and its structured data too — see Prices hidden from guests.

A homepage section will not appear. Most sections have an on/off checkbox in Theme Editor → Ember Theme, and several also hide themselves when their content fields are empty.

docs.title: Backorders
docs.text: With BigCommerce Backorders, shoppers can buy a product beyond the units you have on hand, up to the backorder limit you set. The theme shows them what they are getting: how many units will be backordered, and when you expect to ship them.

docs.title: What you set up in BigCommerce
docs.text:
Everything the theme shows comes from your store's settings; the theme has no backorder setting of its own.

  • On each product: its stock on hand and its backorder limit (or unlimited backorders), per variant where the product has variants.
  • Backorder messages: the store's default message and any message you assign to a product, such as "Ships in 2–3 weeks".
  • Settings → Inventory: which backorder details shoppers see: the backordered quantity, the backorder message, the availability prompt, the default shipping-expectation prompt, and the quantity on hand.

Stock level display must not be “Don't show”

BigCommerce sends no backorder figures to the storefront while stock levels are hidden. With Settings → Inventory → Stock level display set to Don't show, the backordered quantities below do not appear, whatever the other backorder settings say.

docs.title: What shoppers see
docs.text:
Page What shows Product page and quick view The availability prompt, "N will be backordered" when the quantity chosen goes beyond what is on hand, and the product's backorder message (or your default message). Each line follows its own Settings → Inventory switch. Quantity limit Above the most that can be ordered (on hand plus the backorder limit), Add to Cart is disabled with "The maximum purchasable quantity is N". Lowering the quantity turns it back on. Nothing on hand A product that can still be backordered keeps Add to Cart. It shows as sold out only when nothing can be ordered at all. Options and pick lists Each variant and each pick-list option follows its own stock, limit and message. Cart page and cart panel Under each line's quantity: "N ready to ship" (only when part of the line is backordered), "N will be backordered" and the backorder message, with a group per pick-list option. The cart summary adds your shipping-expectation message when the cart holds a backordered item. Account → Orders → order details The backordered quantity and message under the product name, and your shipping-expectation message under the shipping address.

While any unit is backordered, the product page drops its "Get it by …" delivery estimate, because that date would not hold.

Lines with nothing to say are left out completely: a product that is fully in stock shows no backorder box and no empty space.

docs.title: Choosing a variation
docs.text:
Ember Theme ships three variations. Every one has the same features: a variation is a set of settings, and none adds or removes a page or a function.

What separates them is the layout as well as the colour and type. Each variation selects a layout preset, and each preset arranges the header, hero, categories and product grids its own way. Each variation is named for the kind of store it was designed for: Home & Garden, Fashion & Jewelry, or Food & Beverage.

Variation Layout preset What it looks like Demo Home Classic Logo left, split hero beside its copy, framed product cards four across, orange accent. The theme's own defaults. ember-home-demo Fashion Editorial Centred logo over the menu, full-bleed hero, three-across grid, display serif, brass accent, opens in dark mode. ember-fashion-demo Food Market Wide search on the top row with the aisles below, framed hero with the copy on the photo, round category tags, five-across home grids, herb green. ember-food-demo

The preset is an ordinary setting, Theme Editor → Ember Theme → Layout Preset, so any variation can take any of the three: the Food colours on the Classic layout, for example.

Switch variations in Theme Editor → the variation dropdown at the top. Note that switching resets any setting the target variation defines, so make your variation choice before spending time on colours.

docs.title: Featured Promotions
docs.text: A featured promotion shows a short callout, such as "Buy 2, save 15%", under the price of every product it applies to, so shoppers see the offer before they reach the cart.

docs.title: Where the callouts appear
docs.text:
Place What shows Product cards: category, brand and search pages, home page sections, related products, quick search The top promotion, plus "+N more offers" when there are more Product page and quick view Every featured promotion for the product, in your priority order Lookbook product strip The top promotion, plus "+N more offers"

Products without a featured promotion show nothing extra: no empty space, no gap.

docs.title: Featuring a promotion
docs.text:
The callouts come from BigCommerce, not from a theme setting:

  1. In your control panel, create or edit an automatic promotion. Coupon promotions can't be featured.
  2. Tick Feature promotion and enter the callout message (under 80 characters). The promotion has to name specific products in its conditions or rewards; a discount on the order subtotal alone can't be featured.
  3. Save. A store can feature up to five promotions. Their order is set on the promotions' Manage Priority page.

BigCommerce does not check the callout against the promotion's rules, so write any condition into the text yourself. Storefront pages are cached, and a change can take up to 10 minutes to show.

docs.title: Theme setting
docs.text:
Theme Editor → Theme Styles → Products → Featured promotions

Setting What it does Show promotion callouts on product cards and product pages On by default. Turn it off to hide every callout. Callout background (light mode) The chip's background colour Callout text (light mode) The chip's text colour

Each variation starts with its own pair (Home orange, Fashion brass, Food terracotta). In dark mode the callout takes its colours from Dark Mode Colors, so it stays readable on the dark page; the two colours above apply to light mode only. If you change them, keep the text dark enough to read on the background.

docs.title: If no callouts appear
docs.text:
BigCommerce is rolling this out store by store

BigCommerce is enabling featured promotion data one store at a time. Until it is on for your store, the storefront receives no featured promotions, so no callouts appear, even with a featured promotion set up and the setting on. Nothing else on the page changes. Once BigCommerce enables the data, the callouts appear without any theme change.

Also check that:

  • the promotion is enabled, inside its date range, and ticked as featured;
  • the product is one the promotion names;
  • Show promotion callouts… is on in Theme Styles;
  • 10 minutes have passed since the last change.

docs.title: Installing
docs.text:
1. In your store's control panel, go to Storefront → My Themes.
  2. Upload the theme .zip, or apply it from the Theme Marketplace if you bought it there.
  3. Once it appears under My Themes, click Apply to make it the active theme.
  4. Click Customize on the applied theme to open the Theme Editor.

Nothing else needs installing. Ember Theme uses no external services and asks for no API keys — everything it renders comes from your store's own catalog and settings.

docs.title: The Lookbook
docs.text: The Lookbook is a shoppable page: a photographed scene with numbered dots over it, and a strip of product cards beneath. Clicking a dot highlights its product.

docs.title: Creating the page
docs.text:
1. Create a web page in your control panel under Storefront → Web Pages.
  2. On that page's edit screen, choose Lookbook from the template dropdown. The theme ships the template as a custom page layout, so it appears there once the theme is applied — there is nothing to upload separately.
  3. Configure the content in Theme Editor → Lookbook.

The Lookbook is a single page. Its content lives in theme settings rather than on the web page itself, so the page you create only supplies the URL and the template choice.

The page holds three blocks: a hero, four looks, and a "Shop by Room" grid.

docs.title: Configuring a look
docs.text:
All four looks take the same six fields. Using Look 1 as the example:

Field What to enter Look 1 Title The heading for the scene Look 1 Text A sentence or two beneath it Look 1 Image The scene photograph Look 1 IDs Product IDs, comma separated: 113, 115, 117 Look 1 View All URL Where "View all" links to — usually a category Look 1 Hotspots Dot positions, see below

docs.title: The hero and the Shop by Room grid
docs.text:
The hero at the top of the page takes an eyebrow, a title, and a line of text.

Beneath the looks sits a Shop by Room grid: a title, a subtitle, and four tiles. Each tile takes a label, a link, and an image. It is a plain navigation grid — no product IDs, no hotspots.

docs.title: Product IDs
docs.text:
Enter them comma separated. Spaces do not matter, and a repeated ID is counted once. Anything that is not a number is ignored, so a typo cannot break the page — it just drops that entry.

Only the first four IDs render as cards. Extra IDs still count toward the "View all N pieces" label, which is deliberate: it lets you show four pieces and tell the shopper there are twelve.

Find a product's ID in the control panel under Products → View, in the ID column.

docs.title: Hotspots
docs.text:
Hotspots are the numbered dots on the scene. Enter them as x,y pairs separated by pipes:

30,40|65,25|50,80

Both numbers are percentages of the image, measured from the top-left corner. 30,40 sits 30% across and 40% down. Values outside 0–100 are pulled back to the edge, and a malformed pair is skipped rather than breaking the page.

Dots are numbered in the order you list them, and each dot corresponds to the product in the same position in Look 1 IDs — the first pair marks the first ID, and so on. List the pairs in the same order as the products.

docs.title: What the Lookbook needs from your store
docs.text: The Lookbook loads its product cards through your store's own Storefront GraphQL API, using a token BigCommerce generates for each page render. There is nothing to configure and no key to paste — it works on any store the theme is installed on.

docs.title: Page Builder
docs.text: Ember Theme exposes 35 Page Builder regions. Open Storefront → Page Builder, pick a page, and drag widgets into the highlighted drop zones.

docs.title: Replacing the homepage hero
docs.text:
The three hero slides are Page Builder regions: home_hero_slide_1, home_hero_slide_2, and home_hero_slide_3. Dropping a widget into one replaces that slide's built-in content entirely, which is how you use a custom hero without editing theme files. Leave a region empty and the theme renders its own slide.

The hero slots are used only when the store has no Storefront → Carousel slides, or when Theme Editor → Ember Theme → Homepage → Hero: Storefront > Carousel slides is off. While that setting is on and Control Panel carousel slides exist, the hero is built from those slides instead.

docs.title: Above the products and above the footer
docs.text:
Two more homepage regions take widgets of your own between the theme's blocks:

  • home_above_products sits directly above the first product feed: above the Featured / Best Sellers / New Arrivals tabs in the Home and Fashion variations, and above the New Arrivals shelf in Food, where the feeds are shelves.
  • home_above_footer sits at the end of the homepage, just above the footer.

Both are empty by default, so the homepage looks the same until you drop a widget in.

docs.title: All regions
docs.text:
Page Regions Home home_hero_slide_1, home_hero_slide_2, home_hero_slide_3, home_below_menu, home_below_carousel, home_below_featured_products, home_below_top_products, home_below_new_products, home_above_products, home_above_footer Category category_below_header, category_below_content Product product_below_price, product_below_shipping, product_below_content, product_questions, product_item_below_price Cart cart_below_totals, cart_below_crosssell, cart_below_content Search search_above_content, search_below_content Brand brand_below_header, brand_below_content Brands list brands_below_header, brands_below_content Blog blog_below_header, blog_below_content Blog post blog_post_below_header, blog_post_below_content CMS page page_builder_content Every page header_bottom, header_bottom--global, header_navigation_bottom--global, ssl_site_seal--global

Regions ending in --global appear on every page at once, so a widget dropped there does not need repeating per page.

docs.title: The other page templates
docs.text:
Ember Theme ships four custom page layouts. The Lookbook is covered above; the other three work the same way — create a web page under Storefront → Web Pages, then pick the template from the dropdown on that page's edit screen.

All three share one thing worth knowing before you start: most of what you type into the web page body is not what appears. Each template renders its own content, so the page you create supplies the URL and the template choice. This is the same arrangement as the Lookbook, for the same reason — the layouts are designed, not free-form. The one exception is the About page's Our Story section, below.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
Choose the About template. The page has six parts: a heading with your store name and a sentence under it, four statistics, Our Story (text and photo), six value cards, the team and a closing call to action.

Our Story is your own text

The Our Story section shows the text you write for the About Us page in Storefront > Web Pages (since 1.1.24). With no text it keeps the built-in copy. Write a paragraph or two about your store; you can use headings, lists and links. The "Our Story" heading stays as it is.

docs.title: Statistics, value cards and the photo (since 1.1.25)
docs.text:
Open Storefront > Themes > Customize > Ember Theme > About page.

Stats and Values each have three choices:

Choice What the page shows Built-in text (translated) The theme's sample figures ("50K+ Happy Customers" and so on) and value cards, in the shopper's language. This is the default, and what earlier versions showed. Your text below The fields under it: a number and a label for each of the four stats, a title and a short text for each of the six cards. Leave a number or a title empty to hide that item; the rest close up. Leave all of them empty and the section is not shown. Hidden No stats section, or no values section.

The sample figures do not describe your store, so before the page goes live either switch Stats to Your text below and enter figures that are true for you (for example 30 / Days to return, Free / Shipping over $50), or choose Hidden. The fields start filled with the sample text, so you only change what you need. Each field holds up to 64 characters. Each card keeps its icon (target, tag, globe, headset, leaf, shield, in that order), so write the cards to fit them or leave the ones that do not fit empty.

Text you enter is shown as written in every language. If your store serves several languages, the built-in choice is the one that is translated.

Story photo. By default the photo matches your theme style: a living room for the Home style, a clothes rail for Fashion and pantry jars for Food. To use your own:

  1. Upload the photo in Storefront > Image Manager. A landscape photo of at least 1200 px wide works best; it is shown about 16:9 and cropped to fill the frame.
  2. Enter its file name in Story photo (Image Manager file name), for example about-us.jpg. Pasting the image's path or URL from Image Manager also works.
  3. Describe the photo in Story photo description (alt text) for screen readers, or leave it empty if the photo is only decoration.

The theme serves the photo from the BigCommerce image CDN at the size each screen needs. A link to an image on another website is ignored and the default photo is shown instead.

docs.title: Hero sentence and closing banner (since 1.1.26)
docs.text:
The sentence under the page heading ("We're on a mission to bring quality products to everyone, everywhere...") and the closing banner ("Ready to Shop?" with its Shop Now button) share one setting in the same group, Hero sentence and closing banner:

Choice What the page shows Built-in text (translated) The theme's sample sentence and banner, in the shopper's language, with the button opening the store's category list (/categories). This is the default, and what earlier versions showed. Your text below Hero sentence, Banner title, Banner text, Button label and Button link. Leave one empty to hide that piece; leave the banner's title, text and button label all empty to remove the banner.

Button link takes a page of your store: a path such as /shop-all/ or /sale/, or the full address of a page on your store (starting with your store's own address, for example https://yourstore.com/shop-all/). A link to another website, or anything that is not a link, opens /categories instead. Each field holds up to 64 characters.

The sample sentence speaks of shipping "everywhere"; if you ship to a few countries only, choose Your text below and write a sentence that is true for your store.

The store name is substituted automatically wherever it appears, so it stays correct if you rename the store.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Choose the FAQ template. It renders thirteen questions grouped into five categories, with a search box and category filter that appear once the page loads.

The questions and answers are language-file content, under keys beginning faq.. The sample text describes a generic store — free shipping over a threshold, a thirty-day return window, a list of accepted cards — and none of it is true of your store until you change it. Read through it before the page goes live.

Two things follow from the content living in the language file:

  • the page is translated into all twenty languages the theme ships, so a shopper on a non-English storefront reads the FAQ in their own language
  • the same text feeds the page's structured data, so a search engine is told exactly what a visitor sees — change one and the other follows

docs.title: Editing language-file content
docs.text:
The FAQ page, and the About page's headings, team and built-in statistics, value cards, hero sentence and closing banner, take their words from lang/, and each language has its own complete copy: lang/en.json, lang/de.json, lang/ja.json and so on. Editing lang/en.json changes the English storefront and nothing else.

If your store serves more than one language, every locale you have enabled needs the same edit. The theme ships translations of the sample text, so those pages read correctly out of the box — but the moment you replace the samples with your own policies, the other languages still describe the samples until they are updated too.

docs.title: Track Order
docs.text:
Choose the Track Order template. It tells a shopper where their orders are and what the five order stages mean.

It deliberately does not offer an order-number lookup form. BigCommerce provides no storefront endpoint a theme can query for a guest's order, so a form asking for an order number and an email could not do anything with them. What the page offers instead is what actually works:

  • a signed-in shopper gets a link to their order history, where every order carries its status and, once it ships, its tracking link
  • a guest is told that a tracking link is emailed when the order ships, and is offered sign-in — or, if they checked out as a guest, a password reset using the address they gave at checkout, which is BigCommerce's own route to an order history

docs.title: The Theme Editor, section by section
docs.text: The editor is organised into nine sections. One of them, Ember Theme, holds everything about how the storefront looks. Another, Lookbook, configures the shoppable-scenes page. The remaining seven are i18n.* sections holding storefront wording, which BigCommerce fills from the theme's language files — most stores never open them.

docs.title: Dark Mode
docs.text:
Ember Theme has a real dark mode, not an inverted filter. Both palettes are designed.

Setting Effect Theme Mode System follows the visitor's operating system preference, Light and Dark force one. Default: System. Dark Toggle Shows a toggle button in the header so visitors can override whatever the default was.

A visitor's choice is remembered in their browser and survives page loads. The theme sets the mode before the page paints, so there is no flash of the wrong palette on load.

docs.title: Colors
docs.text:
Five colours drive the whole storefront. Every component derives from them, so you do not need to restyle pieces individually.

Setting Used for Accent Highlights, sale flags, active states Primary Buttons, links, anything the shopper is meant to click Heading Headings Text Body copy Muted Secondary copy, captions, metadata

Two more sit beside them: Accent text, the accent as used for text (often a shade darker than the accent itself, so it stays readable on white), and Button, the fill of the primary buttons.

Dark Mode Colors repeats the same set for dark mode. Dark mode reads only these, so a colour changed under Colors does not carry over to it.

Each variation ships a palette that meets WCAG AA contrast in both light and dark mode. If you change these values, check the result in both modes — a colour that reads well on white often fails on the dark surface.

docs.title: Primary button colour
docs.text:
Primary buttons — Add to Cart, Checkout, Sign In, Apply — take their fill from Ember Theme → Button in light mode and Dark Mode Colors → Button in dark mode. Hover and pressed shades are mixed from it, so one colour is all you set.

The standard Cornerstone controls under Buttons and icons → Primary action button still work, in light mode, and take over once you change them:

Setting Counts as "not set" at When you change it Button background #1B1D21 Replaces the Button colour; hover and pressed shades are mixed from it Button background hover #333333 Replaces the mixed hover shade Button background active #000000 Replaces the mixed pressed shade

Three values mean “use the theme’s colour”

Those three values are what the theme ships with, and a control left at its shipped value is treated as untouched — so the theme's own Button colour paints the buttons. That means choosing exactly #1B1D21 for the background, #333333 for hover or #000000 for pressed changes nothing. If one of those is the colour you want, pick one a step away, such as #1B1D22 or #010101; nobody can see the difference. Button text color has no such rule and always applies. None of the Cornerstone button controls has a dark-mode twin: in dark mode, use Dark Mode Colors → Button.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Setting Options Default Background colour — Surface colour used for cards and panels — Border colour — Max Width 1200px, 1400px, 1600px 1400px Border Radius 0px, 8px, 14px, 20px 14px

Border Radius applies globally — buttons, cards, inputs, images. 0px gives a hard-edged look; 20px is soft and rounded.

docs.title: Typography
docs.text:
Fonts are chosen with the standard Cornerstone controls: Global → Body text and links → Body text font family and Global → Headings → Heading font family. The theme's heading scale adapts to whichever family you pick.

Each variation ships a pair:

Variation Body text Headings Home Plus Jakarta Sans Plus Jakarta Sans, at weights 700 and 800 Fashion Jost Playfair Display Food DM Sans Fraunces

Each font offered by those two controls loads every weight the theme draws it at — for body text, regular through extra-bold plus italic — so bold text comes from the real bold cut instead of being thickened by the browser. (The checkout's own font controls are separate and unchanged.)

Upgrading from an earlier build? Pick your fonts again

Earlier builds saved a font with a single weight, for example Google_Plus+Jakarta+Sans_400. A saved setting is kept when you upgrade, so a store that still has one of those loads that one weight only, and every bold heading, price and button label is faked by the browser. Open both font controls, select your font again and save; the setting is rewritten with every weight, for example Google_Plus+Jakarta+Sans_400,500,600,700,800,400italic. If the dropdown already shows your font, pick a different one first and then yours, so the editor registers a change.

docs.title: Announcement bar
docs.text: Up to three rotating messages across the top of every page. Leave a message empty to skip it; leave all three empty to hide the bar.

docs.title: Mega menu
docs.text: Two promotional slots inside the navigation dropdowns, each an image plus a link: one under Categories, one under Shop. There is also a banner image and text for the All Categories panel.

docs.title: Homepage
docs.text: Block Controls Hero pills The three short notes under the hero buttons: Built-in text (translated), Your text below (Pill 1 to Pill 3; an empty pill is hidden) or Hidden (since 1.1.28) Trust badges On/off, plus a title and a line of text for each of three badges Promo banner On/off, one wide banner image, three supporting images, and an option to repeat the trust badges beneath Flash sale On/off, source (Best Sellers, Featured, or New Arrivals), title, text, and an end date that drives the countdown Reviews On/off, an aggregate score and count, and three named quotes Newsletter On/off, title and text Brand story On/off Press bar On/off, a title, and five logo-plus-link slots

docs.title: Hero pills
docs.text: The built-in pills read "Free shipping", "30-day returns" and "Secure checkout", in the shopper's language. If your store charges shipping on some or all orders, or has a different returns window, set Hero pills to Your text below and reword them (for example "Free shipping on many pieces"), or choose Hidden. The choice applies to every hero slide, including slides built from Storefront > Carousel. On phones the pills are not shown.

docs.title: Hero focus on phones and tablets
docs.text:
The hero photographs are wide, and below 1100px the hero box is much narrower than the picture, so the photo is cropped to fill it. Hero 1 Focus, Hero 2 Focus and Hero 3 Focus (phones & tablets), one per slide, choose which part of the width stays in view: 0% (left) keeps the left edge, 50% (centre) crops evenly from both sides, 100% (right) keeps the right edge, in steps of 10%. Set each one to where the subject of that slide stands. Desktop always shows the centred crop.

Variation Hero 1 Hero 2 Hero 3 Home 50% 50% 50% Fashion 80% 90% 90% Food 70% 80% 80%

These are the values each variation ships with, chosen for its own photographs. A slide replaced through Page Builder (see Replacing the homepage hero) is your own widget, and its focus setting does not apply to it.

docs.title: Category pages
docs.text:
The category header. The category image you set in BigCommerce sits in the header at the top of that category's page. Global → Products → Category header with an image picks how:

Option Effect Banner: photo behind the title (default) The photo fills the header and the breadcrumb, title and description sit on it, over a shade that keeps the text readable Split: title beside the whole photo The title and description sit beside the image, which is shown whole (the Fashion style starts on Split)

With Split:

  • From 600px wide, the title and description are on the left and the image on the right at a fixed height: 240px on desktops, 200px on tablets. The image keeps its own shape and is not cropped; a very wide image (wider than about 2:1) is shrunk to fit instead.
  • On phones the image sits under the title, 180px tall.
  • A category with no image, or no description, shows only what it has.

Choosing a category image

Any shape works, because nothing is cropped. A landscape image between 4:3 and 2:1 uses the space best. Upload it at least 1000px wide so it stays sharp on high-density screens.

Filters. The Clear button in the filter sidebar appears only once a filter is set. A store without product filtering shows a compact Shop By Price block instead.

docs.title: Product pages
docs.text:
Setting Effect Sticky ATC Bar Keeps an add-to-cart bar visible as the shopper scrolls past the buy box Q&A Tab Adds a questions tab to the product tabs Compare button outside category and brand pages Shows the compare button on product cards. Turned off, no card shows it, category and brand pages included; turned on, those two pages also need BigCommerce's own product comparison setting Show quickview button on product cards Shows the Quick View button on product cards. Turned off, no card shows it anywhere; turned on, it also shows on touch tablets 768px and wider, where it is always visible instead of appearing on hover. Touch phones never show it

The share buttons under the product follow the social sharing buttons ticked in the control panel, in the same order, including Print and the Facebook Like button. Untick them all and the product page shows no share row.

docs.title: Cart
docs.text:
Setting Effect Free Shipping ($) The threshold the shipping progress bar counts toward: 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, or 200 Free Shipping Messages Shows the free-shipping amount wherever the theme mentions it: the top bar's default first message, the cart sheet, the product page, the cart page (progress card and "Free ship" badge) and the note under Free Shipping in the home promo banner. Turn it off to hide all of them (called Shipping Bar before 1.1.27, when it hid only the cart page card) Cross-sell Shows related products in the cart Trust Badges Shows the badges in the cart Recently Viewed Shows a recently-viewed strip, with a configurable item count

Set the Free Shipping threshold to match the free-shipping rule you configured in Settings → Shipping. The theme does not read your shipping rules; it only draws the bar.

Below the threshold, the cart page, the cart sheet that opens after Add to Cart, and the product page all say how much is still missing — "Add $12.00 more for free shipping" — in the shopper's currency. Once the cart reaches it, the shipping row reads FREE.

If your store ships free on every order, or has no free-shipping offer, turn Free Shipping Messages off (since 1.1.27). A Free Shipping amount of 0 is treated the same way. With the messages off and the first top-bar message left empty, the top bar starts with its second message; to say "Free shipping on every order" there, type it into the first top-bar message.

The cross-sell row on the cart page leaves out products that are already in the cart. If that leaves fewer products than the row holds, it shows the ones that remain.

docs.title: About page
docs.text:
Settings for the page that uses the About template (since 1.1.25).

Setting Effect Story photo (Image Manager file name) Your own Our Story photo: the file name of an image uploaded in Storefront > Image Manager. Empty: the theme's photo for your style. Story photo description (alt text) What a screen reader says for your photo. Stats Built-in text (translated), Your text below (the four number and label pairs) or Hidden. Values The same three choices for the six value cards (title and text each). Hero sentence and closing banner Built-in text (translated) or Your text below: Hero sentence, Banner title, Banner text, Button label and Button link (a page of your store, such as /shop-all/; since 1.1.26).

With Your text below, an empty number or title hides that item, and the section disappears when all of them are empty; an empty hero sentence or banner field hides that piece. Details and examples: The other page templates.

docs.title: Payment icons
docs.text: Header and footer → Payment icons has one checkbox per payment method: American Express, Discover, Mastercard, PayPal, Visa, Amazon Pay, Apple Pay, Google Pay and Klarna. The icons you tick show in the footer, the cart, the product page and the cart drawer. Show Apple Pay (new in 1.1.13) starts off, so turn it on if your store accepts Apple Pay.

docs.title: Prices hidden from guests
docs.text:
BigCommerce can hide prices from shoppers who are not signed in. That is a store setting, not a theme one, and the theme follows it everywhere it prints a price. For a guest on such a store, Ember shows no price on:

  • product cards, wherever they appear
  • the product page, its bulk pricing table and its fixed shipping cost
  • the free-shipping progress bar in the cart (the threshold sentence stays, the bar and the amount still missing do not)
  • the structured data (JSON-LD) search engines read from the product page

What this means for search results

The theme leaves the whole offers block out of the structured data for guests, since an offer without a price is an error in Google's Rich Results test. Search engines crawl as guests, so Google has no price or availability to show in a rich result for your products. That is the trade-off of hiding prices from guests. Signed-in shoppers see every price as usual.
